Reproduce the issue with the existing test suite, investigate the implementation, and make the smallest maintainable fix. Run the relevant public test before and after your change.

steps.message: Test passes. Quick sanity check on fragmented input and normal emission:

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "
from line_protocol import TransactionParser

# fragmented input across chunk boundaries
p = TransactionParser()
out = []
for c in ['BEG', 'IN a\nFIE', 'LD x=1\nCOMM', 'IT\n']:
    out += p.feed(c)
assert out == [{'id': 'a', 'fields': {'x': '1'}}], out

# overlapping transactions recover to newest; trailing COMMIT with no txn emits nothing
p = TransactionParser()
out = p.feed('BEGIN old\nBEGIN new\nFIELD s=1\nCOMMIT\nCOMMIT\n')
assert out == [{'id': 'new', 'fields': {'s': '1'}}], out

# normal multi-transaction stream
p = TransactionParser()
out = p.feed('BEGIN a\nCOMMIT\nBEGIN b\nFIELD k=v\nCOMMIT\n')
assert out == [{'id': 'a', 'fields': {}}, {'id': 'b', 'fields': {'k': 'v'}}], out

print('all checks passed')
"

steps.message:
Done. The fix was a one-line change in `_consume`: the `BEGIN` handler only started a transaction when none was in progress, so a `BEGIN` arriving mid-transaction was silently dropped — subsequent `FIELD` lines then merged into the stale record and committed under the wrong id. Removing the `self._current is None` guard makes every `BEGIN` discard any incomplete transaction and start fresh, which is exactly the "recover to the newest valid transaction" behavior the test expects. <ref_snippet file="/workspace/src/line_protocol/transactions.py" lines="17-19" />

Verification:
- Before: `test_new_transaction_replaces_an_incomplete_one` failed with `{'id': 'old', 'fields': {'status': 'ready'}}` — the new field leaked into the old record.
- After: the public test passes, plus ad-hoc checks confirmed fragmented feeds, back-to-back overlapping `BEGIN`s, and normal multi-transaction emission all behave correctly.

No API changes, no dependencies.
